elements.label: Figure S3.5
elements.title: National standards bodies are more likely to participate in the development of international standards in the technology and innovation sector as country income level increases
elements.content: Chart type: Horizontal 100% stacked bar chart. X-axis: Share of national standards participated in, by sector (%), ranging from 0 to 100. Y-axis: Country income groups (HICs, UMICs, LMICs, LICs). Legend/Series: Technology and innovation, Science and environment, Infrastructure and transport, Health and food systems, Governance and safety. Data values per group: HICs: Technology and innovation = 57, Science and environment = 19, Infrastructure and transport = 3, Health and food systems = 10, Governance and safety = 12. UMICs: Technology and innovation = 54, Science and environment = 20, Health and food systems = 13, Governance and safety = 14 (Infrastructure and transport not explicitly labeled on bar). LMICs: Technology and innovation = 50, Science and environment = 16, Health and food systems = 24, Governance and safety = 10. LICs: Technology and innovation = 41, Science and environment = 17, Health and food systems = 34, Governance and safety = 7. Source: WDR 2025 team, based on administrative data as of 2024 provided by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). Note: Constituent percentages for each country income group may not sum exactly to 100 percent as a result of rounding. HICs = high-income countries; LICs = low-income countries; LMICs = lower-middle-income countries; UMICs = upper-middle-income countries.
